verdict: 2026-07-26 09:54:31 PDT — I would build the production change this way: it uses the existing rate-limit dependency declaratively, localizes Railway-specific IP handling, keeps sanitization small, and avoids unnecessary OAuth/deauth changes. One test-design concern remains. The gate was inconclusive because the enforced read-only sandbox blocked Vitest temporary files, network listeners, and mkdtemp—not because assertions failed.

findings.title: Rate-limit tests exercise the dependency, not the custom IP policy
findings.claim: All three tests use the default socket address, so they verify express-rate-limit's established counting behavior but never exercise the branch-owned clientIpKey policy. The accepted design's central invariant—requests sharing X-Real-IP share a bucket while another client retains its own bucket—could break or collapse all clients together without failing these tests.
findings.alternative: Replace the low-value default-burst test with one integration test that sends X-Real-IP: A until A is limited, then sends X-Real-IP: B and confirms B still succeeds. Include an IPv6 value if normalization is an intended invariant.
findings.win: Tests the only custom and deployment-specific part of the limiter, removes one dependency-behavior test, and guards against both cross-client starvation and ineffective per-IP limiting.
